moment.reason: Moment.js is in maintenance mode and is 289KB+ minified. Modern alternatives are much smaller.

alternatives.name: dayjs
alternatives.note: Drop-in replacement with same API, 99% smaller

alternatives.name: date-fns
alternatives.note: Functional approach, only import what you use

alternatives.name: luxon
alternatives.note: By Moment team, modern immutable API

lodash.reason: Most lodash utilities have native JS equivalents. Full lodash is 72KB minified.

alternatives.name: lodash-es
alternatives.note: ESM version — bundlers only include what you import

alternatives.name: native JS
alternatives.note: Array.find, Object.entries, optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??) cover most use cases

underscore.reason: Underscore is largely superseded by native JS methods and lodash.

alternatives.name: native JS
alternatives.note: Modern JS covers most underscore utilities

alternatives.name: radash
alternatives.note: Modern utility library if you need one

request.reason: Deprecated since February 2020. No longer receives security patches.

alternatives.name: undici
alternatives.note: Node.js native HTTP client, fastest option

alternatives.name: ky
alternatives.note: Tiny, elegant HTTP client by Sindre Sorhus

node-fetch.reason: Native fetch() is stable in Node.js 18+ since 2022. No need for a polyfill.

axios.reason: Consider lighter alternatives if you only need basic HTTP requests.

alternatives.name: native fetch
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 18+, handles most use cases

alternatives.name: ky
alternatives.note: Tiny fetch wrapper with retries, timeouts, JSON shortcuts

alternatives.name: ofetch
alternatives.note: Universal fetch by UnJS, works everywhere

colors.reason: Had a supply chain sabotage incident in Jan 2022. Use maintained alternatives.

alternatives.name: colorette
alternatives.note: Tiny and fast terminal color library

faker.reason: Original faker was sabotaged and abandoned. Use the community fork.

uuid.reason: Node.js and browsers have built-in UUID generation since 2021.

alternatives.name: crypto.randomUUID()
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 19+ and all modern browsers

rimraf.reason: Node.js fs.rm() with recursive option is built-in since Node 14.

alternatives.name: fs.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 14+, no dependency needed

mkdirp.reason: Node.js fs.mkdir() with recursive option is built-in since Node 10.

alternatives.name: fs.mkdir(path, { recursive: true })
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 10+, no dependency needed

left-pad.reason: String.padStart() is built into all modern JS engines.

glob.reason: Consider built-in Node.js fs.glob (Node 22+) or faster alternatives.

bluebird.reason: Native Promises are fully featured in modern Node.js. Bluebird's perf advantage is gone.

alternatives.name: native Promise
alternatives.note: V8's native Promise is now faster than Bluebird

alternatives.name: p-map / p-limit
alternatives.note: If you need concurrency control, use focused utilities

chalk.reason: chalk is solid but consider lighter alternatives if you only need basic colors.

alternatives.name: picocolors
alternatives.note: 14x smaller, 2x faster, covers basic use cases

alternatives.name: colorette
alternatives.note: Tiny and fast, good middle ground

moment-timezone.reason: Moment-timezone is 900KB+ with timezone data. Modern alternatives are much smaller.

alternatives.name: dayjs + timezone plugin
alternatives.note: Same API, fraction of the size

alternatives.name: Intl.DateTimeFormat
alternatives.note: Built-in browser/Node API for timezone formatting

node-sass.reason: Deprecated in favor of Dart Sass. Node-sass is unmaintained and has native binding issues.

alternatives.name: sass
alternatives.note: Official Dart Sass, pure JS, actively maintained

enzyme.reason: Enzyme is abandoned and doesn't support React 18+. Use modern testing utilities.

alternatives.name: @testing-library/react
alternatives.note: Community standard for React testing, supports React 18+

classnames.reason: Consider smaller alternatives or template literals for simple use cases.

alternatives.name: clsx
alternatives.note: Same API as classnames, 2x smaller and faster

body-parser.reason: Built into Express.js 4.16+ as express.json() and express.urlencoded().

alternatives.name: express.json()
alternatives.note: Built into Express 4.16+, no separate install needed

dotenv.reason: Node.js 20.6+ has built-in --env-file flag for .env loading.

alternatives.name: node --env-file=.env
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 20.6+, no dependency needed

cross-env.reason: Modern Node.js and npm scripts handle cross-platform env vars better now.

alternatives.name: cross-env
alternatives.note: Still useful if supporting older Node or complex env setups

express-validator.reason: Consider lighter validation libraries if you don't need Express middleware integration.

joi.reason: Joi is large (145KB) and primarily server-side. Modern alternatives are smaller and more universal.

yup.reason: Consider newer, smaller validation libraries with better TypeScript support.

async.reason: Native async/await and Promise utilities replace most of the async library's functionality.

querystring.reason: Node.js built-in querystring module is deprecated. Use URLSearchParams.

alternatives.name: URLSearchParams
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js and browsers, standard API

alternatives.name: qs
alternatives.note: If you need nested object support

path-to-regexp.reason: URLPattern is now available in Node.js 23+ and most browsers.

alternatives.name: URLPattern
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 23+ and modern browsers

isomorphic-fetch.reason: fetch() is now built into both Node.js 18+ and all modern browsers.

alternatives.name: native fetch
alternatives.note: Built into Node.js 18+ and all modern browsers

whatwg-fetch.reason: fetch() polyfill is no longer needed — all modern browsers support it natively.

core-js.reason: Most core-js polyfills are unnecessary if targeting modern browsers/Node.js.

alternatives.name: Check browserslist
alternatives.note: Review your target browsers — you may not need polyfills

alternatives.name: core-js-pure
alternatives.note: Non-polluting version if you still need polyfills

winston.reason: Consider lighter logging libraries if you don't need Winston's full transport system.

bunyan.reason: Bunyan is largely unmaintained. Modern alternatives are faster and lighter.

superagent.reason: Superagent is older and larger than modern HTTP client alternatives.

alternatives.name: playwright
alternatives.note: By Microsoft, supports all browsers, actively maintained

protractor.reason: Protractor has been deprecated since Angular 15.

tslint.reason: TSLint was deprecated in 2019 in favor of ESLint with TypeScript support.

q.reason: Q Promise library is obsolete — native Promises are built into JavaScript.

when.reason: when.js Promise library is unmaintained — native Promises are the standard.

backbone.reason: Backbone.js is from 2010 and effectively unmaintained.

bower.reason: Bower has been deprecated since 2017 in favor of npm/yarn.

grunt.reason: Grunt is largely superseded by npm scripts and modern build tools.

alternatives.name: npm scripts
alternatives.note: Built into npm, no task runner needed

alternatives.name: turborepo
alternatives.note: If you need advanced task orchestration

gulp.reason: Gulp is losing adoption to modern bundlers and npm scripts.

alternatives.name: vite
alternatives.note: Modern build tool with excellent DX

immutable.reason: Immutable.js adds significant bundle weight. Consider lighter approaches.

alternatives.name: immer
alternatives.note: Work with immutable state using normal JS syntax

alternatives.name: structuredClone()
alternatives.note: Built-in deep clone for simple immutability

rxjs.reason: RxJS is powerful but heavy (42KB). Consider if you really need reactive streams.

alternatives.name: native EventTarget
alternatives.note: Built-in event system for simple pub/sub

alternatives.name: mitt
alternatives.note: Tiny event emitter if you just need pub/sub

is-odd.reason: You really don't need a package for n % 2 !== 0.

is-even.reason: You really don't need a package for n % 2 === 0.

is-number.reason: typeof n === 'number' or Number.isFinite(n) does the same thing.

is-string.reason: typeof s === 'string' does the same thing.
